review_candidates.description: PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE The Regional Geophysicist is responsible for planning, supervising, and interpreting geophysical surveys (magnetic, electrical/IP, and radiometric) to support orogenic gold exploration in West African terranes. The role focuses on delivering high‑quality datasets, robust QA/QC, and integrated geophysical–geological interpretations to advance exploration targets and drill decisions. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES Survey design and data acquisition Contribute to survey design for ground and/or airborne magnetic, electrical/IP, and radiometric programs in orogenic gold settings. Prepare technical specifications, layouts, and parameter tests in collaboration with project geologists and external contractors. Supervise or closely monitor data acquisition to ensure adherence to survey design, HSE standards, and contractual requirements. Provide real‑time technical support to field geophysicists and crews, including troubleshooting of acquisition and positioning issues. Data QA/QC and management Develop and implement QA/QC procedures including but not restricted to magnetic, electrical/IP, and radiometric datasets (line checks, repeatability, noise assessment, positioning control, base station corrections, etc.). Review daily production, observer logs, and preliminary products to ensure data quality before survey demobilization. Validate contractor deliverables against technical specifications and quality standards and manage non‑conformance follow‑up where required. Ensure secure, well‑structured data management (raw, processed, and metadata), including naming conventions, audit trails, and transfer to corporate databases. Processing and basic products Process geophysical data using industry‑standard software to generate robust, reproducible basic products (e.g., reduced‑to‑pole and derivative magnetic grids, radiometric ratio maps, IP chargeability/resistivity sections and grids). Apply appropriate filters, corrections, and leveling techniques suitable for West African orogenic gold terrains and acquisition geometry. Document processing workflows and parameters so that products can be independently reproduced and reviewed. Generate clear map and section products at appropriate scales, with consistent symbology and cartographic standards ready for geological interpretation. Geological integration and interpretation Work closely with project geologists to link geophysical responses to lithology, structure, alteration, and mineralization styles typical of West African orogenic gold systems. Participate in interpretation sessions and targeting workshops, integrating geophysics with geology, geochemistry, drilling, and structural models. Develop and maintain 2D/3D geophysical interpretation layers (structures, domains, target corridors) that can be used directly for drill, trench, or follow‑up survey planning. Communicate the uncertainty, limitations, and alternative explanations of geophysical responses, and propose additional data or tests where required. Remote sensing and value‑add Where applicable, incorporate remote sensing products (e.g., multispectral/shortwave infrared alteration mapping, DEM/terrain analysis, lineament extraction) as a complementary layer to geophysical and geological datasets. Contribute to the evaluation of new remote sensing and geophysical tools or workflows that may improve target definition in orogenic gold environments. Stakeholder communication and reporting Prepare concise technical reports, memos, and presentations that clearly summarize survey objectives, methods, QA/QC, processing, and key interpretation outcomes. Present results and recommendations to exploration management, geology teams, and other stakeholders in a clear, decision‑oriented format. Support budget estimates, schedules, and scopes of work for future geophysical programs SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE Required qualifications and experience Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Geophysics Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in applied geophysics, preferably in mineral exploration with exposure to orogenic gold systems. Strong practical experience with magnetic, electrical/IP, and radiometric methods, from acquisition principles through to processing and basic interpretation. Demonstrated ability to relate geophysical responses to geology (lithology, alteration, structure, and mineralization controls) in hard‑rock terrains. Experience working with cross‑functional exploration teams in African or similar remote environments. Technical skills Proficiency with one or more geophysical processing/interpretation packages (e.g., Oasis montaj, VOXI, IP/resistivity inversion tools, equivalent). Solid understanding of survey design, sampling, and noise sources for magnetic, electrical/IP, and radiometric methods. Competence in GIS and map preparation (e.g., ArcGIS/QGIS) for integrating geophysical products with geology and geochemistry. Familiarity with remote sensing datasets and workflows (e.g., Sentinel/Landsat, commercial multispectral, DEM analysis) is a strong plus. Good data management discipline, including handling of large raster/vector datasets and clear documentation of workflows Behavioural competencies Strong collaboration skills and willingness to work in close partnership with geologists, field teams, and contractors. Clear, structured communication, both written and verbal, tailored to technical and non‑technical audiences. Proactive approach to identifying data quality issues, proposing solutions, and continuously improving workflows. Resilience and adaptability to field‑based work rhythms, changing priorities, and remote‑area challenges. CONTRACT TYPE: LONG TERM
